102	
103	3. **Run the four attack lenses.** For each, generate findings:
104	
105	   **a. Build-vs-buy alignment**
106	   - Did the planner ignore a "buy: <X>" recommendation and re-create what X does? → critical.
107	   - Did the planner adopt "buy: <X>" but still include stories that duplicate X's coverage? → important.
108	   - Did the planner pick "build" when the researcher said "buy" without naming why? → critical.
109	
110	   **b. Riskiest-assumption check**
111	   - For each epic, what does the plan assume "just works"? (Auth flows. Wire shapes. Third-party APIs. Browser compatibility. Migration paths.)
112	   - For each assumption: is it actually verified, or is it inherited from "we did this last time"? Inherited-without-verification on a load-bearing assumption is critical.
113	
114	   **c. Hidden-complexity check**
115	   - Stories that touch ≥4 files (or aren't sized but obviously will) → split it (important).
116	   - Stories whose AC says "works" or "is fast" without a measurable threshold → tighten the AC (important).
117	   - Cross-process I/O (HTTP, SSE, WebSocket, IPC, file format) without a wire-contract acceptance criterion in the relevant story → critical (this is the bug class CSI-526..531 came from).
118	   - Persistence without a migration story → important.
119	   - Auth/authorization without a dedicated story → critical.
120	
121	   **d. User-journey check**
122	   - Does the plan let a user actually use the product end-to-end after the listed stories ship? Or are pieces missing (deploy, login, settings, the "first run" path)?
123	   - If the answer is "not until the last 2 stories", the plan probably has dependency ordering wrong → important.
124	   - If the answer is "never, this plan is mid-journey only", → critical (scope clarification needed before user approval).
125	
126	4. **Tag every finding with severity.**
127	   - **Critical** — the plan should not be shown to the user as-is. Loop back to planner.
128	   - **Important** — the plan can go to the user, but flag this so they can opt in/out.
129	   - **Nice-to-have** — would improve the plan; one-line note is enough.
130	
131	5. **Decide the verdict.**
132	   - Any critical findings → **LOOPBACK**. Orchestrator re-spawns the planner with the critical findings.
133	   - No critical, ≥1 important → **SURFACE**. Orchestrator shows plan + your report to user.
134	   - No findings worth raising → **CLEAR**. Orchestrator shows plan to user with one-line "challenger cleared".
135	
136	6. **Compress the report.** Token budget: ~800-1200. If you have 7 critical findings, the plan was probably bad and the planner needs the full list — don't truncate criticals. Cut nice-to-haves first if you must.

140	- **Adversarial, not negative.** Every finding must include a concrete recommendation, not just "this seems risky". A finding without a fix is not a finding.
141	- **One severity per finding.** If you're torn between critical and important, default to important — overusing critical desensitizes the loopback signal.
142	- **Don't reinvent the planner.** You are not rewriting the plan. You are flagging gaps. The planner owns the rewrite.
143	- **Don't second-guess the researcher.** If the researcher recommended "buy: assistant-ui" and you disagree, that's a separate workstream — note it as a `nice-to-have` only. The build-vs-buy decision is the researcher's domain; your job is plan-vs-research alignment, not re-running the survey.
144	- **No code reads beyond the manifest + CLAUDE.md.** You're reviewing the plan, not the code. Stack constraints from the manifest are fair game; deep code reads are out of scope.
145	- **No Jira calls.** Phase 1.5 runs before tickets exist. Do NOT use any `mcp__mcp-atlassian__*` tool. Do NOT load them via ToolSearch.
146	- **One question to the user max.** If a finding genuinely needs the user to choose (e.g., "build-vs-buy verdict is split, planner picked build, do you want to revisit?"), surface it once at the top of your `## Summary`. The orchestrator presents this alongside the plan.
147	- **Verdict is binding on the orchestrator.** If you say LOOPBACK, the planner re-runs. If you say SURFACE, the user sees it. If you say CLEAR, the plan goes through with a one-line note.

If the line `Self-Learning: OFF` is present, **omit this entire `## Lessons` section** from your return text — do not emit any `### Lesson` block regardless of in-flow friction. 153	If during your run you:
154	- Retried a tool/command after a failure and the second-or-later attempt succeeded
155	- Worked around a non-obvious problem (missing env var, wrong path, contract mismatch with an artifact you read)
156	- Discovered something that contradicts your role definition or an artifact you read
157	- Found that a sibling artifact (tech spec, design spec, integration notes) was wrong or incomplete
158	
159	…then append a `## Lessons` section to your final return text. Each lesson is one block:
160	
161	```
162	### Lesson
163	Trigger: <one sentence — what happened>
164	Generalizable rule: <one sentence — phrased imperatively, what should always/never happen>
165	Suggested fix type: <instruction-edit | memory-feedback | hook | skill | script | slash-command | manual>
166	Suggested target: <file path or artifact, your best guess — extractor may override>
167	```
168	
169	If your run had no friction worth a lesson, omit the section entirely. If something IS covered by your role definition but still caused friction — that's a red flag worth reporting (the definition may be unclear, outdated, or not being followed).

276	The Python package is `jiralyzer_web/` under `web/backend/`. It serves the
277	React SPA's static assets and the `/api/*` JSON / SSE endpoints from a single
278	uvicorn process. DuckDB is opened read-only at request time. Pins, dashboards,
279	and conversations are persisted as JSON files under `~/.jiralyzer/`. The chat
280	agent calls the Anthropic API via tool-use with SQL execution and schema tools.
281	
282	```mermaid
283	flowchart LR
284	  User[Browser] -->|HTTP / SSE| FastAPI
285	  User -->|Streamlit alt| Streamlit
286	  subgraph CLI
287	    Sync[jiralyzer sync] --> DB
288	    Ingest[jiralyzer ingest] --> DB
289	  end
290	  subgraph Backend
291	    FastAPI -->|read-only| DB[(DuckDB)]
292	    FastAPI --> Pins[(Pins JSON)]
293	    FastAPI --> Dash[(Dashboards JSON)]
294	    FastAPI --> Conv[(Conversations JSON)]
295	    FastAPI -->|chat tool-use| Anthropic[Anthropic API]
296	  end
297	  Streamlit -->|read-only| DB
298	  Streamlit --> Pins
299	```
300	
301	ASCII fallback and full notes: [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).
302	
303	### Environment Variables
304	
305	All variables use the prefix `JIRALYZER_`; values may also live in a `.env`
306	file in the working directory.
307	
308	| Var | Purpose | Default |
309	|---|---|---|
310	| `JIRALYZER_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | Anthropic API key — required for chat / agent loop | unset → chat disabled |
311	| `JIRALYZER_WEB_TOKEN` | Optional bearer-token gate for protected `/api/*` | unset → app is open |
312	| `JIRALYZER_DB_PATH` | DuckDB file path | `jiralyzer.db` |
313	| `JIRALYZER_PINS_DIR` | Pinned-analyses directory (shared with Streamlit) | `~/.jiralyzer/analyses/` |
314	| `JIRALYZER_CONV_DIR` | Conversation history directory | `~/.jiralyzer/conversations/` |
315	| `JIRALYZER_DASHBOARDS_DIR` | Dashboard layouts directory | `~/.jiralyzer/dashboards/` |
316	| `JIRALYZER_MODEL` | Anthropic model override | `claude-sonnet-4-6` |
317	| `JIRALYZER_GRAFANA_URL` | Grafana base URL for chat-driven dashboards | `http://localhost:3000` |
318	| `JIRALYZER_GRAFANA_TOKEN` | Grafana service-account token | unset → Grafana tools disabled |
319	| `JIRALYZER_GRAFANA_DATASOURCE_UID` | UID of the provisioned DuckDB datasource | `afpaugs0xmakgb` |
320	| `JIRALYZER_CUSTOM_FIELDS_MAP` | Custom-field → column promotion map | `run.sh` defaults to `config/csi_custom_fields_map.yaml`; packaged default `src/jiralyzer/custom_fields_map.yaml` is empty |
321	
322	### Custom-Field Promotion — CSI instance config
323	
324	Promoted custom-field columns (`team`, `csi_teams`, `in_quarter_plan`, `quarter`,
325	`zone`, …) are **critical** to the app, the chat agent, and the Grafana sprint
326	drill-down. They are defined in **`config/csi_custom_fields_map.yaml`** (git-tracked,
327	CSI deployment config) and loaded via `JIRALYZER_CUSTOM_FIELDS_MAP`, which `run.sh`
328	points there by default.
329	
330	**Why not in the packaged default?** `src/jiralyzer/custom_fields_map.yaml` ships
331	with the package and must stay **empty/generic** so the product promotes cleanly
332	(`product_files_identical` rule) — a test (`test_packaged_default_when_no_env`)
333	enforces it loads to `{}`. The CSI mapping has its own regression test
334	(`test_csi_instance_map_loads_expected_columns`) guarding the 16 expected columns.
335	To add/rename a promoted column: edit `config/csi_custom_fields_map.yaml`, update
336	that test, then re-sync/ingest (promotion is idempotent + additive).
337	
338	### Commands
339	
340	```bash
341	uv run jiralyzer web                    # build SPA (if needed) + start on :8000
342	uv run jiralyzer web --reload --build   # dev mode: hot-reload + force rebuild
343	uv run jiralyzer web --port 9000 --no-open
344	uv run jiralyzer dashboard              # legacy Streamlit (still works)
345	```

348

350	uv run python -m jiralyzer_web

359	```

361	### Model Rationale
362	
363	Default model is **Claude Sonnet 4.6** — chosen for the cost/quality balance
364	on the tool-use SQL agent loop. Override with `JIRALYZER_MODEL` (any
365	`claude-*` model id supported by the Anthropic SDK).
366	
367	### Streamlit Coexistence
368	
369	The Streamlit dashboard and the web app both read DuckDB read-only via the
370	DuckDB shared file lock; they can run simultaneously on different ports. All
371	writes happen via the CLI (`jiralyzer sync` / `jiralyzer ingest`) — never from
372	a request handler. Pinned analyses are stored in the same JSON directory and
373	are visible to both UIs.
374	
375	### Productionization
376	
377	Multi-user SSO and hosted deployment are tracked under **CSI-430** and are
378	explicitly out of scope for the web-app MVP. The current default
379	(`JIRALYZER_WEB_TOKEN` unset) targets single-user local development.
380	
381	### Sub-package documentation
382	
383	- Backend: [`web/backend/README.md`](web/backend/README.md) — module layout,
384	  endpoint catalog, auth, tests.
385	- Frontend: [`web/frontend/README.md`](web/frontend/README.md) — Vite + React
386	  scaffold, Zscaler `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` note, scripts.

388	## Grafana Integration
389	
390	A local Grafana reads the same DuckDB **read-only** for solid, filterable
391	graph dashboards alongside the webapp/Streamlit. Setup lives under `grafana/`
392	(provisioning + launch/sync scripts) — see `grafana/start-grafana.sh`.
393	
394	- **Read-only is mandatory.** The DuckDB datasource path uses
395	  `?access_mode=read_only` so Grafana takes a shared lock; otherwise it grabs
396	  an exclusive write lock that blocks `jiralyzer sync`. A writer still needs the
397	  file alone — run `grafana/sync-window.sh` (stops Grafana → sync → restarts).
398	- **Chat-driven dashboards.** The chat agent can author Grafana dashboards via
399	  the `create_grafana_dashboard` and `list_grafana_dashboards` tools
400	  (`web/backend/jiralyzer_web/agent/tools.py`). The dashboard JSON is built by
401	  `web/backend/jiralyzer_web/grafana.py` (`build_dashboard`), which mirrors the
402	  hand-authored dashboard: query-type filter variables + a null-safe
403	  `('__all__' IN ($var) OR col IN ($var))` gate spliced in at a `{filters}`
404	  token. Each panel's SQL is dry-run against the DB before the dashboard is
405	  pushed, so bad queries fail fast instead of rendering empty panels.
406	- **Enable it.** Set `JIRALYZER_GRAFANA_TOKEN` (a Grafana service-account
407	  token) — tools are hidden/disabled when unset. Create the service account
408	  once: `POST /api/serviceaccounts` (Editor) → `POST
409	  /api/serviceaccounts/{id}/tokens`.
410	- **Allowed filter columns:** project, issue_type, status, priority, assignee,
411	  reporter, resolution (restricted to prevent SQL-identifier injection).
412	- **Grafana Cockpit (`/grafana`, epic CSI-588).** The webapp serves an
413	  additive cockpit route at `:8000/grafana` — a chrome-less Grafana embed on the
414	  left, assistant-ui chat on the right, no filter sidebar. The `/` 3-pane app is
415	  untouched; reach the cockpit via the **Grafana** link in the header nav. It
416	  needs the anon-Viewer + `allow_embedding` `grafana.ini` config (CSI-589, see
417	  `grafana/README.md`). The dashboard picker reads `GET /api/grafana/dashboards`
418	  (never 500s — `{enabled:false}` → graceful "not configured" state). Chat-
419	  authored dashboards auto-focus the embed (CSI-592). The embed is **theme-
420	  synced** (CSI-593): the app theme (`useThemeStore`) is baked into the iframe
421	  `&theme=dark|light`; Grafana 13.x has no postMessage theme API, so a toggle
422	  recomputes the `src` and the iframe is keyed on `${uid}-${theme}` to force a
423	  clean reload. Local-dev single-user scope only (multi-user under CSI-430).
424	
425	### CSI Sprint Dashboard & Drill-down
426	
427	The hand-authored **CSI Sprint Dashboard** (`grafana/dashboards/csi_sprint_dashboard.py`,
428	Grafana uid `csi-sprint-june-2026`) replicates Jira dashboard 12354: one row per
429	team, each with SP / Tickets / Missing-Info stat panels. Every per-team stat has
430	**field-level drill-down links** into a shared generic issue table
431	(`grafana/dashboards/sprint_drilldown.py`, detail uid `sprint-issues`).
432	
433	**Sprint metric definitions (must match exactly when reproducing numbers):**
434	- **Sprint membership:** `custom_fields.field_name = 'customfield_10020'`, value
435	  like `CSI_Q226_Sprint6_310526`. The **`sprints` table** (synced from Jira
436	  Agile API during `jiralyzer sync`) holds `start_date` / `end_date` keyed by
437	  sprint `name`. Grafana uses hidden query variables `$sprint_start` /
438	  `$sprint_end` that auto-derive from `$sprint` via the sprints table.
439	- **"Done" is window-scoped, NOT just `status='Done'`:** a ticket counts as done
440	  only if `status IN ('Done')` **AND** it transitioned to Done within
441	  `[sprint_start, sprint_end]` (a `status_changes` subquery). Plain
442	  `status='Done'` over-counts (it includes earlier-sprint completions).
443	- **planned** = `in_quarter_plan = 'Yes'`. **unplanned** =
444	  `(project='CSIPLN' AND in_quarter_plan='No') OR project='CREQ'`.
445	- **`csi_teams` is THE sole team filter** (replaces old `team`/`it_service`/
446	  `assignee` triple-OR). It is a comma-separated multi-value field — match
447	  with regex/LIKE, never `=`. Tokens: `Devops, Security, HD, DCOps, Network,
448	  VSO, SOS, FinOps, Arch`. Bulk-populated via `/tmp/bulk_csi_teams.py` from
449	  `customfield_11067` in Jira (CSI-TEAMS checkbox field).
450	
451	**Drill-down design + gotchas:**
452	- The detail table is generic, driven by URL/template vars: `team` (regex),
453	  `plan`, `status` (multi), `sprint`, plus `assignee`/`issue_type`/`priority`
454	  refine filters and a hidden `missing` mode (`none|plan|quarter|canceled`) for
455	  the Missing-Info panel's data-quality fields.
456	- The agent's built-in `create_grafana_dashboard` drill-down (`col IN ($var)`)
457	  CANNOT reproduce these windowed/JOIN measures — that's why this is a bespoke
458	  detail table mirroring each panel's WHERE clause, not the generic feature.
459	- Multi-select **"All" sentinel must be quoted** (`allValue = "'__all__'"`); an
460	  unquoted `__all__` makes `'__all__' IN ($var)` read a bare column → zero rows.
461	- Data links append **`&kiosk=1`** so the linked dashboard stays chrome-less in
462	  the cockpit embed (Grafana doesn't propagate kiosk across navigation).
463	- A two-value stat tile (done + total) only reliably exposes ONE clickable
464	  link; split into two single-value panels if both must be clickable.
465	- **`sprint_drilldown.py` is idempotent — re-run it after any rebuild.** Running
466	  `csi_sprint_dashboard.py` rebuilds all panels and WIPES the drill-down links;
467	  re-running `sprint_drilldown.py` restores them across all 9 team rows.
468	- **Source of truth is Grafana's saved JSON, NOT the build scripts.** Manual
469	  layout edits happen in the Grafana UI. Future changes MUST use the
470	  read-modify-write pattern (`/tmp/grafana_patch.py`): GET → mutate → POST
471	  (pop `id` + `version` before saving). Never full-rebuild unless intentionally
472	  resetting.
473	
474	## Git Conventions
475	
476	- **Remote:** `origin` = `final-israel/jiralyzer`. Push only here (`git push`
477	  works as-is; `dev` tracks `origin/dev`). Never push to `final-il` (kept as
478	  `final-il-old`; its push path is blocked).
479	- **Security gate:** `final-israel` runs **Cycode** on push — secret detection
480	  (no static tokens/credential headers, even in tests — build them at runtime)
481	  and SCA/SAST. Pushes that introduce secrets or vuln deps are flagged.
482	- Branches: `main` (prod), `dev` (development)

484	- Push code changes to `dev` branch, merge to `main` when proven

489	- **Plotly HTML blank behind Zscaler:** Both CDN and inline (`include_plotlyjs=True`) produce blank pages. Charts default to PNG (Matplotlib). Use `--output chart.html` only on non-proxy networks.
490	- **Jira `/rest/api/3/search` deprecated (410 Gone):** Using GET `/rest/api/3/search/jql` with `nextPageToken` pagination instead.
491	- **Story points field varies by instance:** Parser auto-detects from `customfield_10016`, `customfield_10034`, `customfield_10028`. API fetches `fields=*all` to ensure custom fields are included.
492	
493	## Team-Based Queries
494	
495	When analyzing tickets by team, always use the CSI team mapping (member names) to find all related tickets — do NOT rely solely on the Jira `team` custom field. Many tickets lack the team field but can be attributed to a team by their assignee or reporter.
496	
497	**Strategy:** For any team-related query, build an `assignee IN (...)` or `reporter IN (...)` filter using all team members' display names. Combine with the `team` field where available using OR logic.

# Jiralyzer — Project Instructions

## Overview

Jira ticket analytics tool. Syncs from Jira REST API into DuckDB, runs SQL queries, generates visualizations. Built as a Python package with a Click CLI + a Claude Code skill. Supports multiple projects in the same DB.

**Repo:** `final-israel/jiralyzer` (private) — this is the canonical remote
(`origin`). Push only here. (`final-il/jiralyzer` exists as `final-il-old` but
its push path is blocked/restricted — do NOT push there.)
**Jira Project:** CSI (key: CSI, board: CSI-PM)
**Default Branch:** `main`

## Tech Stack

- **Python >=3.11**, managed with `uv` (never bare pip)
- **DuckDB** — local analytical database, single file
- **Click** — CLI framework
- **Matplotlib** — static PNG charts (default, works behind Zscaler)
- **Plotly** — interactive HTML charts (blank behind Zscaler TLS proxy)
- **requests + truststore** — Jira REST API client with SSL proxy support
- **Hatchling** — build backend, src layout
- **pytest + ruff** — testing and linting (93 tests, 90% coverage)
- **Streamlit** — interactive web dashboard (`./run.sh dashboard`)
- **streamlit-autorefresh** — file-mtime polling for live updates

## Input Format Decision (2026-04-14)

**JSON only: Jira REST API JSON** (`expand=changelog`)
- All 6 tables populated: tickets, status_changes, assignments, comments, custom_fields, worklogs
- Bulk export: Python script calls REST API with pagination, saves to `export.json`
- Incremental: `jiralyzer sync --since <date>` fetches deltas via API

**Why not RSS XML?** Jira Cloud's RSS export lacks changelogs and worklogs — only tickets + comments + custom_fields. Not worth maintaining a second parser for a strict subset. Can add later if needed.

Data flow:
```
First time:  jiralyzer sync --project KEY          (full sync via REST API)
Updates:     jiralyzer sync --project KEY --since <date>  (incremental delta)
Alt:         jiralyzer ingest export.json           (from saved JSON file)
```

## Commands

```bash
uv sync                              # Install dependencies
uv run pytest -v                     # Run tests
uv run ruff check src/               # Lint
uv run jiralyzer sync --project KEY  # Fetch from Jira REST API + ingest
uv run jiralyzer ingest <path>       # Parse JSON/XML export into DuckDB
uv run jiralyzer query "<sql>"       # Run SQL query
uv run jiralyzer schema              # Show schema
uv run jiralyzer stats               # Summary statistics
uv run jiralyzer chart "<sql>" ...   # Generate chart
uv run jiralyzer export-parquet <d>  # Export to Parquet
```

```

├── README.md
├── pyproject.toml              # uv + hatchling, Python >=3.11

### Pinned Analyses Storage

7 DuckDB tables — see `src/jiralyzer/schema.sql` for DDL:
- `tickets` — one row per Jira ticket (26 columns + generated `resolution_days`)
- `status_changes` — from changelog items where field='status' (JSON only)

## Web App

The FastAPI + React/TS web app under `web/` is the modern UI for Jiralyzer.
It coexists with the Streamlit dashboard — both work simultaneously, both read
DuckDB read-only — and adds an agentic chat panel for natural-language
analytics on top of the same data.

### Architecture

The Python package is `jiralyzer_web/` under `web/backend/`. It serves the
React SPA's static assets and the `/api/*` JSON / SSE endpoints from a single
uvicorn process. DuckDB is opened read-only at request time. Pins, dashboards,
and conversations are persisted as JSON files under `~/.jiralyzer/`. The chat
agent calls the Anthropic API via tool-use with SQL execution and schema tools.

```mermaid

  User[Browser] -->|HTTP / SSE| FastAPI
  User -->|Streamlit alt| Streamlit
  subgraph CLI
    Sync[jiralyzer sync] --> DB
    Ingest[jiralyzer ingest] --> DB
  end
  subgraph Backend
    FastAPI -->|read-only| DB[(DuckDB)]
    FastAPI --> Pins[(Pins JSON)]
    FastAPI --> Dash[(Dashboards JSON)]
    FastAPI --> Conv[(Conversations JSON)]
    FastAPI -->|chat tool-use| Anthropic[Anthropic API]
  end
  Streamlit -->|read-only| DB
  Streamlit --> Pins
```

ASCII fallback and full notes: [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md).

file in the working directory.

### Custom-Field Promotion — CSI instance config

Promoted custom-field columns (`team`, `csi_teams`, `in_quarter_plan`, `quarter`,
`zone`, …) are **critical** to the app, the chat agent, and the Grafana sprint
drill-down. They are defined in **`config/csi_custom_fields_map.yaml`** (git-tracked,
CSI deployment config) and loaded via `JIRALYZER_CUSTOM_FIELDS_MAP`, which `run.sh`
points there by default.

**Why not in the packaged default?** `src/jiralyzer/custom_fields_map.yaml` ships
with the package and must stay **empty/generic** so the product promotes cleanly
(`product_files_identical` rule) — a test (`test_packaged_default_when_no_env`)
enforces it loads to `{}`. The CSI mapping has its own regression test
(`test_csi_instance_map_loads_expected_columns`) guarding the 16 expected columns.
To add/rename a promoted column: edit `config/csi_custom_fields_map.yaml`, update
that test, then re-sync/ingest (promotion is idempotent + additive).

## Grafana Integration

A local Grafana reads the same DuckDB **read-only** for solid, filterable
graph dashboards alongside the webapp/Streamlit. Setup lives under `grafana/`
(provisioning + launch/sync scripts) — see `grafana/start-grafana.sh`.

- **Read-only is mandatory.** The DuckDB datasource path uses
  `?access_mode=read_only` so Grafana takes a shared lock; otherwise it grabs
  an exclusive write lock that blocks `jiralyzer sync`. A writer still needs the
  file alone — run `grafana/sync-window.sh` (stops Grafana → sync → restarts).
- **Chat-driven dashboards.** The chat agent can author Grafana dashboards via
  the `create_grafana_dashboard` and `list_grafana_dashboards` tools
  (`web/backend/jiralyzer_web/agent/tools.py`). The dashboard JSON is built by
  `web/backend/jiralyzer_web/grafana.py` (`build_dashboard`), which mirrors the
  hand-authored dashboard: query-type filter variables + a null-safe
  `('__all__' IN ($var) OR col IN ($var))` gate spliced in at a `{filters}`
  token. Each panel's SQL is dry-run against the DB before the dashboard is
  pushed, so bad queries fail fast instead of rendering empty panels.
- **Enable it.** Set `JIRALYZER_GRAFANA_TOKEN` (a Grafana service-account
  token) — tools are hidden/disabled when unset. Create the service account
  once: `POST /api/serviceaccounts` (Editor) → `POST
  /api/serviceaccounts/{id}/tokens`.
- **Allowed filter columns:** project, issue_type, status, priority, assignee,
  reporter, resolution (restricted to prevent SQL-identifier injection).
- **Grafana Cockpit (`/grafana`, epic CSI-588).** The webapp serves an
  additive cockpit route at `:8000/grafana` — a chrome-less Grafana embed on the
  left, assistant-ui chat on the right, no filter sidebar. The `/` 3-pane app is
  untouched; reach the cockpit via the **Grafana** link in the header nav. It
  needs the anon-Viewer + `allow_embedding` `grafana.ini` config (CSI-589, see
  `grafana/README.md`). The dashboard picker reads `GET /api/grafana/dashboards`
  (never 500s — `{enabled:false}` → graceful "not configured" state). Chat-
  authored dashboards auto-focus the embed (CSI-592). The embed is **theme-
  synced** (CSI-593): the app theme (`useThemeStore`) is baked into the iframe
  `&theme=dark|light`; Grafana 13.x has no postMessage theme API, so a toggle
  recomputes the `src` and the iframe is keyed on `${uid}-${theme}` to force a
  clean reload. Local-dev single-user scope only (multi-user under CSI-430).

### CSI Sprint Dashboard & Drill-down

The hand-authored **CSI Sprint Dashboard** (`grafana/dashboards/csi_sprint_dashboard.py`,
Grafana uid `csi-sprint-june-2026`) replicates Jira dashboard 12354: one row per
team, each with SP / Tickets / Missing-Info stat panels. Every per-team stat has
**field-level drill-down links** into a shared generic issue table
(`grafana/dashboards/sprint_drilldown.py`, detail uid `sprint-issues`).

**Sprint metric definitions (must match exactly when reproducing numbers):**
- **Sprint membership:** `custom_fields.field_name = 'customfield_10020'`, value
  like `CSI_Q226_Sprint6_310526`. The **`sprints` table** (synced from Jira
  Agile API during `jiralyzer sync`) holds `start_date` / `end_date` keyed by
  sprint `name`. Grafana uses hidden query variables `$sprint_start` /
  `$sprint_end` that auto-derive from `$sprint` via the sprints table.
- **"Done" is window-scoped, NOT just `status='Done'`:** a ticket counts as done
  only if `status IN ('Done')` **AND** it transitioned to Done within
  `[sprint_start, sprint_end]` (a `status_changes` subquery). Plain
  `status='Done'` over-counts (it includes earlier-sprint completions).
- **planned** = `in_quarter_plan = 'Yes'`. **unplanned** =
  `(project='CSIPLN' AND in_quarter_plan='No') OR project='CREQ'`.
- **`csi_teams` is THE sole team filter** (replaces old `team`/`it_service`/
  `assignee` triple-OR). It is a comma-separated multi-value field — match
  with regex/LIKE, never `=`. Tokens: `Devops, Security, HD, DCOps, Network,
  VSO, SOS, FinOps, Arch`. Bulk-populated via `/tmp/bulk_csi_teams.py` from
  `customfield_11067` in Jira (CSI-TEAMS checkbox field).

**Drill-down design + gotchas:**
- The detail table is generic, driven by URL/template vars: `team` (regex),
  `plan`, `status` (multi), `sprint`, plus `assignee`/`issue_type`/`priority`
  refine filters and a hidden `missing` mode (`none|plan|quarter|canceled`) for
  the Missing-Info panel's data-quality fields.
- The agent's built-in `create_grafana_dashboard` drill-down (`col IN ($var)`)
  CANNOT reproduce these windowed/JOIN measures — that's why this is a bespoke
  detail table mirroring each panel's WHERE clause, not the generic feature.
- Multi-select **"All" sentinel must be quoted** (`allValue = "'__all__'"`); an
  unquoted `__all__` makes `'__all__' IN ($var)` read a bare column → zero rows.
- Data links append **`&kiosk=1`** so the linked dashboard stays chrome-less in
  the cockpit embed (Grafana doesn't propagate kiosk across navigation).
- A two-value stat tile (done + total) only reliably exposes ONE clickable
  link; split into two single-value panels if both must be clickable.
- **`sprint_drilldown.py` is idempotent — re-run it after any rebuild.** Running
  `csi_sprint_dashboard.py` rebuilds all panels and WIPES the drill-down links;
  re-running `sprint_drilldown.py` restores them across all 9 team rows.
- **Source of truth is Grafana's saved JSON, NOT the build scripts.** Manual
  layout edits happen in the Grafana UI. Future changes MUST use the
  read-modify-write pattern (`/tmp/grafana_patch.py`): GET → mutate → POST
  (pop `id` + `version` before saving). Never full-rebuild unless intentionally
  resetting.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Jiralyzer Setup Script
# Run once to configure the environment. After this, the jiralyzer skill is ready.

set -euo pipefail

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
YELLOW='\033[1;33m'
NC='\033[0m'

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
ENV_FILE="$SCRIPT_DIR/.env"
PASS=0
FAIL=0

pass() { echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓${NC} $1"; PASS=$((PASS + 1)); }
fail() { echo -e "  ${RED}✗${NC} $1"; FAIL=$((FAIL + 1)); }
warn() { echo -e "  ${YELLOW}!${NC} $1"; }
header() { echo -e "\n${YELLOW}--- $1 ---${NC}"; }

# ─── Step 1: uv ───

header "Step 1: Check uv"

if command -v uv &>/dev/null; then
    pass "uv installed ($(uv --version))"
else
    warn "uv not found. Installing..."
    curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
    export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
    if command -v uv &>/dev/null; then
        pass "uv installed ($(uv --version))"
    else
        fail "uv installation failed. Install manually: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/"
        echo -e "\n${RED}Cannot continue without uv.${NC}"
        exit 1
    fi
fi

# ─── Step 2: .env file ───

header "Step 2: Environment configuration (.env)"

if [[ -f "$ENV_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "  Found existing .env file. Checking values..."
    set -a && source "$ENV_FILE" && set +a
else
    echo "  No .env file found. Let's create one."
    echo ""
fi

prompt_var() {
    local var_name="$1"
    local description="$2"
    local default_value="${3:-}"
    local current_value="${!var_name:-}"

    if [[ -n "$current_value" ]]; then
        pass "$var_name = $current_value"
        return
    fi

    if [[ -n "$default_value" ]]; then
        read -r -p "  $var_name ($description) [$default_value]: " value
        value="${value:-$default_value}"
    else
        read -r -p "  $var_name ($description): " value
    fi

    if [[ -z "$value" ]]; then
        fail "$var_name is required"
        return
    fi

    export "$var_name=$value"
    pass "$var_name = $value"
}

prompt_var JIRA_URL "Jira instance URL" ""
prompt_var JIRA_EMAIL "Jira API user email" ""
prompt_var JIRA_API_TOKEN "Jira API token" ""
prompt_var REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE "CA certificate bundle for Python requests" "/Library/CompanyCA/zscaler-root.pem"
prompt_var UV_SSL_CERT_FILE "CA certificate bundle for uv/pip" "$HOME/.config/uv/ca-bundle.pem"
prompt_var JIRALYZER_PROJECT_DIR "Jiralyzer project directory" "$SCRIPT_DIR"
prompt_var JIRALYZER_DB_PATH "DuckDB database file path" "$SCRIPT_DIR/jiralyzer.db"
prompt_var JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR "Chart output directory" "$SCRIPT_DIR/charts"

# Write .env file
echo ""
echo "  Writing .env file..."
cat > "$ENV_FILE" << ENVEOF
# Jiralyzer Environment Configuration
# Generated by setup.sh on $(date +%Y-%m-%d)

# --- Jira API Credentials (required) ---
JIRA_URL=$JIRA_URL
JIRA_EMAIL=$JIRA_EMAIL
JIRA_API_TOKEN=$JIRA_API_TOKEN

# --- SSL / Proxy (required behind corporate proxy) ---
REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE=$REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE
UV_SSL_CERT_FILE=$UV_SSL_CERT_FILE

# --- Jiralyzer Paths ---
JIRALYZER_PROJECT_DIR=$JIRALYZER_PROJECT_DIR
JIRALYZER_DB_PATH=$JIRALYZER_DB_PATH
JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR=$JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR
ENVEOF
pass ".env file written to $ENV_FILE"

# ─── Step 3: SSL cert ───

header "Step 3: SSL certificates"

if [[ -f "$REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE" ]]; then
    pass "REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE exists at $REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE"
else
    fail "REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE not found at $REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE"
fi

if [[ -f "$UV_SSL_CERT_FILE" ]]; then
    pass "UV_SSL_CERT_FILE exists at $UV_SSL_CERT_FILE"
else
    fail "UV_SSL_CERT_FILE not found at $UV_SSL_CERT_FILE"
    echo -e "  ${RED}uv sync will fail without this cert.${NC}"
fi

# ─── Step 4: Python dependencies ───

header "Step 4: Install Python dependencies (uv sync)"

cd "$JIRALYZER_PROJECT_DIR"
if [[ -f ".venv/bin/python3" ]]; then
    pass ".venv already exists"
else
    warn ".venv not found. Running uv sync..."
fi

echo "  Running uv sync..."
if SSL_CERT_FILE="$UV_SSL_CERT_FILE" uv sync 2>&1; then
    pass "uv sync completed"
else
    fail "uv sync failed"
fi

# ─── Step 5: Verify jiralyzer CLI ───

header "Step 5: Verify jiralyzer CLI"

if cd "$JIRALYZER_PROJECT_DIR" && uv run jiralyzer --version &>/dev/null; then
    pass "jiralyzer CLI works ($(uv run jiralyzer --version 2>&1))"
else
    fail "jiralyzer CLI not responding"
fi

# ─── Step 6: Chart directory ───

header "Step 6: Chart output directory"

mkdir -p "$JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR"
if [[ -d "$JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR" ]]; then
    pass "Chart directory ready: $JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR"
else
    fail "Could not create chart directory: $JIRALYZER_CHART_DIR"
fi

# ─── Step 7: Test Jira connectivity ───

header "Step 7: Test Jira API connectivity"

echo "  Checking connection to $JIRA_URL..."
HTTP_CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
    --cacert "$REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE" \
    -u "$JIRA_EMAIL:$JIRA_API_TOKEN" \
    "$JIRA_URL/rest/api/3/myself" 2>/dev/null || echo "000")

if [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "200" ]]; then
    pass "Jira API connection successful"
elif [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "401" ]]; then
    fail "Jira API auth failed (401). Check JIRA_EMAIL and JIRA_API_TOKEN."
elif [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "000" ]]; then
    fail "Cannot reach $JIRA_URL. Check JIRA_URL and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE."
else
    fail "Jira API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
fi

# ─── Summary ───

header "Summary"
echo ""
echo -e "  ${GREEN}Passed: $PASS${NC}"
if [[ $FAIL -gt 0 ]]; then
    echo -e "  ${RED}Failed: $FAIL${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${RED}Fix the failures above and re-run: ./setup.sh${NC}"
    exit 1
else
    echo -e "  ${RED}Failed: 0${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo -e "  ${GREEN}✓ Jiralyzer is ready! The skill can now analyze Jira data.${NC}"
    echo ""
    echo "  Next: ask Claude to analyze a Jira project, e.g.:"
    echo "    \"analyze CREQ project tickets\""
    exit 0
fi

"""Application settings driven by environment variables.

All variables are read with the prefix ``JIRALYZER_`` (case-insensitive).
A ``.env`` file in the working directory is loaded if present. Unknown
variables are ignored so adding new env vars never breaks startup.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path

from pydantic import SecretStr, field_validator
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    """Runtime configuration for the Jiralyzer web backend."""

    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(
        env_prefix="JIRALYZER_",
        env_file=".env",
        extra="ignore",
        case_sensitive=False,
    )

    db_path: Path = Path("jiralyzer.db")
    model: str = "claude-sonnet-4-6"
    anthropic_api_key: SecretStr | None = None
    web_token: SecretStr | None = None
    conv_dir: Path = Path.home() / ".jiralyzer" / "conversations"
    dashboards_dir: Path = Path.home() / ".jiralyzer" / "dashboards"
    # Bind to loopback by default: the API surface (raw SQL, the LLM agent) is
    # open when JIRALYZER_WEB_TOKEN is unset, so it must not be reachable off-host
    # without an explicit opt-in. Set JIRALYZER_HOST=0.0.0.0 to expose it (and set
    # a token when you do).
    host: str = "127.0.0.1"
    port: int = 8000

    # Grafana integration — lets the chat agent author Grafana dashboards.
    # Disabled (tools hidden) unless both url and token are set.
    grafana_url: str = "http://localhost:3000"
    grafana_token: SecretStr | None = None
    grafana_datasource_uid: str = "afpaugs0xmakgb"

    @field_validator("web_token", "grafana_token", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def _empty_token_is_none(cls, v: str | None) -> str | None:
        """Treat empty string as unset (prevents lockout / accidental enable)."""
        if v == "":
            return None
        return v


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    """Return the cached :class:`Settings` singleton."""

    return Settings()

It runs *inside a user's Claude Code session*, against the CLI/DB — it is not a service the server hosts. On a server it must authenticate to *something* (Bedrock proxy URL + creds, or Anthropic key) — and the current code has two competing defaults. Shipping without resolving this means chat is broken or misconfigured on first deploy.

The `/api/*` surface includes raw SQL execution and an autonomous LLM agent. The plan has no story for auth, exposure, or TLS.

A naive `docker compose up` on a server either binds loopback (unreachable) or exposes an unauthenticated SQL/LLM endpoint. CSI-430 (multi-user SSO) is explicitly out of scope and unresolved — so the plan ships an open door or an unreachable app.

- **What's wrong:** 2.1 covers Zscaler CA "both stages." But the *runtime* CA need is broader: `jiralyzer sync` hits Jira over the proxy (`REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` + `truststore`), the agent's LLM calls go through the proxy, and Grafana's plugin install at build also needs it. Separately, the app image story (2.1) lists "web+CLI+sync+streamlit" in one image — Streamlit is a second long-running server (`jiralyzer dashboard`) that the compose (2.3) never assigns a service/port.
- **Why it matters:** If the target server isn't behind Zscaler, baking the CA is harmless; if it is, missing it on any one path (sync, LLM, plugin install) is a silent TLS failure. And an image that "runs streamlit" with no compose service means Streamlit ships but never starts.
- **Recommendation:** Make CA handling a runtime concern, not just build (mount/env the bundle, make path configurable per the Zscaler-vs-not open question). Decide Streamlit's fate explicitly: drop it (web app supersedes it) or give it a compose service + port. Don't ship a dead binary.

- **What's wrong:** 4.1–4.3 build a forward-only SQL migrator with a migrate-then-serve gate; 4.4 adds backup/restore. But the user's ask centers on "upgrades." The plan has no AC that exercises an actual version-N→N+1 upgrade against a *populated* DB (the rebuild-table idiom on a multi-GB synced DB is the risk), and no rollback story beyond "restore a backup."
- **Why it matters:** Forward-only migration on the real CSI DB is where upgrades break — a failed mid-migration leaves a half-migrated single-file DB with no transactional rollback in the plan.
